A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WavefrontDiffusion and retain matching methods and experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, BERTScore measurements, MHCO analysis, hyperparameter experiments, and a decoding case study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds benchmark, backbone, baseline, robustness, calibration, and decoding-dynamics evaluations.

M1.justification: The default scoring, selection, expansion, and pruning procedure in Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 is unchanged. Appendix C.5 adds evaluated variants using entropy or the top-two probability margin instead of maximum probability for token priority, modifying one component of the procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 1 add MBPP to the existing code-generation coverage. GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, BBH, and WikiText remain; the added backbone and diagnostic experiments do not introduce another domain or dataset.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained Standard Diffusion and BlockDiffusion comparisons, Table 9 adds Truncated-BlockDiffusion, Running Confidence Remasking, and Self-Speculative Decoding. Table 14 also evaluates Autoregressive Greedy decoding. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds Dream-7B evaluations, denoising budgets of 256 and 512 steps, stochastic temperatures, teacher-forced calibration with ECE/MCE, and throughput and latency comparisons. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original deterministic 1024-step benchmark settings remain.

E4.justification: v1 already includes F/R sensitivity, MHCO analysis, and the Fibonacci case study. Appendices C.3–C.5 and C.7–C.8 add denoising-step and temperature sensitivity, alternative-priority ablations, calibration diagnostics, frontier evolution, confidence heatmaps, and post-finalization stability analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 explicitly reports means and standard deviations over three random seeds for the temperature experiment. v1 already reports BERTScore uncertainty, which is retained unchanged; v3 does not establish an increase in repetitions for those earlier results.

E6.justification: Original benchmark entries and Tables 2–8 are retained, while Table 1 adds MBPP and Dream-7B results and Tables 9–15 add extensive comparison and diagnostic results. New findings include WavefrontDiffusion scoring 42.38 versus BlockDiffusion's 43.14 at 256 steps, but 73.79 versus 67.02 at 512 steps on GSM8K.

T1.justification: v1 provides mathematical descriptions of decoding but no optimality theorem. Section 3.1 and Appendix D introduce an Information Gradient Assumption relating entropy to distance, a restricted-search framework, and a theorem with a proof sketch asserting inclusion of lowest-entropy candidates for a sufficient wavefront radius.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same headline claims about training-free adaptive scheduling, improved accuracy and semantic fidelity, compute parity, and MHCO. The expanded experiments support these existing claims; these sections still describe four benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations involving entropy-distance structure, filtering poorly calibrated tokens, reduced finalization regret, robustness to priority choice, and compatibility with caching and speculative acceleration. These extend the mechanism and applicability discussion considerably, while the existing calibration and long-context limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code repository URL on the title page; v1 only promises a subsequent public release. The existing hardware, software, prompts, and default hyperparameter documentation in Appendices A–B remains unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the availability or completeness of its contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused references and discussion concerning MBPP, Truncated-BlockDiffusion, MDPO/RCR, Self-Speculative Decoding, and Fast-dLLM. Appendix C distinguishes the method from adaptive competitors and positions it as compatible with acceleration techniques. The broader related-work discussion in Section 5 is unchanged.

P1.justification: The title corrects 'or' to 'for'; author information is reformatted, acknowledgements are added, and selected theory and experimental paragraphs are expanded. Appendices C–D extend the document, but the existing section sequence and most retained prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains MBPP columns and a Dream-7B block. New Tables 9–15, six-panel calibration Figure 3, and three-panel dynamics Figure 4 substantially expand the visual presentation. Table 2 is relocated, and the title page and conference headers are reformatted; the original figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone, benchmark, dynamic baselines, and controlled ablations address v1's limited evaluation breadth. However, new calibration values disagree between Table 15 and Figure 3, including opposite GSM8K MCE trends. Table 14's latency is also unreconciled with Table 10's throughput. These conflicts undermine important new mechanism and efficiency evidence, so the expanded coverage does not establish a reliable net improvement in overall quality.
